page: Amazon Web Services m8g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 64 physical cores on the ARM64 architecture using the Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 model running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated with one thread per core, supported by 64 KB L1D cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. No GPUs are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 7394.64 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 224.93 GB/sec. Multi-core capabilities are strong, as evidenced by top-tier scores in Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU physics, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, with Redis achieving 131.7 million operations per second. Single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, falls in the average tier.

Utilizing the ARM64 architecture, the m8g.16xlarge offers high resource density and power efficiency typical of Graviton-based hardware, making it a cost-effective option for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of x86 licensing. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and exceptional multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, this server is highly suited for database operations, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale multi-threaded applications.

Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server provides a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but contains no local storage or GPU accelerators. Conversely, single-core metrics remain in the average tier. This hardware profile delivers qualitative cost efficiency through ARM-based resource density, making it highly suitable for multi-threaded workloads, database hosting, static web serving, and software development pipelines.
